What it's caught in production
False “confirmed bugs” stopped before escalation. A batch of tickets that read as confirmed backend issues from ledger data alone turned out, checked live, to be mostly unverifiable or already explained by policy. None were wrongly promised to a customer or filed to engineering.
Hidden reward exclusions surfaced. A “missing reward” that the ledger alone made look like a bug was actually a policy exclusion, and the same check caught a second exclusion on the account the customer hadn't even flagged.
Cross-ticket pattern detection. Two unrelated customers, weeks apart, hit the identical undocumented milestone-delay pattern, invisible to two agents working their own queues in isolation.
Self-corrects its own knowledge base. When a rule turned out wrong, such as a customer message wrongly assumed to be Kiwi-originated, it was corrected in place and explained, not just patched for one ticket.
Verifies every conclusion against live systems before a reply goes out. Human sign-off retained on every send.

How I think about customer operations

Principles, not tactics. These guide every decision I make.

01
Automate repetitive work before hiring more people
Identify the 20% of issue types driving 80% of tickets. Automate those first. Headcount is a last resort, not a first response.
02
Fix root causes, not ticket volume
A rising queue is a product signal. I treat support as an insight engine and use it to push upstream fixes that eliminate contact entirely.
03
Use AI to reduce effort, not accountability
Deploy AI where answers are deterministic. Keep humans where judgment matters. Never use automation to avoid ownership.
04
Treat support as a strategic data source
Every ticket is signal. I build systems that surface patterns and translate them directly into product roadmap inputs, with evidence, not anecdote.
05
Measure every process by cost, speed, and impact
If I can't quantify it, I don't trust it. Metrics attached to every initiative from day one: CSAT delta, resolution time, deflection rate.
06
Build infrastructure that outlasts you
SOPs, QA frameworks, escalation paths: systems designed to run at quality regardless of who is on shift. Durability over dependency.

Project Dobby

An AI investigator that works a support ticket the way a senior agent would: it checks every claim against live systems before it drafts a reply.

Why it was built

Fintech support tickets rarely say what is really wrong. Answering from the ticket text alone meant wrong guesses about payments, rewards or card status, and a second ticket from an unhappy customer.

What it does

Reads the ticket, works out who the customer is, and pulls live evidence from production data, the data warehouse, product analytics and payment gateways. It matches the SOP for the question actually asked and drafts the reply. A person approves every reply before it is sent.

Benefits and advantages

  • Replies rest on live facts, not on what the ticket text claims
  • Send guards stop wrong product names, wrong statuses and missing identifiers before anything goes out
  • Every correction becomes a rule, so a mistake is made once
  • A separate grader scores runs pass or fail against live systems
  • A person keeps the final say on every reply

Horus

Dobby rebuilt as a team of AI agents, so a whole queue of tickets can be worked in one run instead of one at a time.

Why it was built

One agent working one ticket at a time could not keep up with bulk buckets, and long runs drifted as the agent's working memory filled up.

What it does

A router sends each ticket to one of 9 workflows. Investigator agents gather evidence in parallel, drafters write the replies, and an independent reviewer checks each draft before a person approves the batch.

Benefits and advantages

  • A whole bucket in one run, up to 20 tickets investigated at once
  • Each workflow loads only its own rules, so agents stay on task
  • The reviewer catches mistakes the first two stages missed
  • Hooks block a send if the text differs from what was approved
  • One send path, so every reply is checked and logged the same way

Project Genie

Closes the loop on open engineering tickets, so customers are not left waiting on an answer that already exists.

Why it was built

Issues escalated to engineering sat open in Jira. Sometimes the team had already answered, sometimes the problem had fixed itself, and either way the customer was still waiting.

What it does

Downloads every open CS Jira with its comments and groups them by root cause. Where the team has answered, it drafts the customer email; where it has not, Dobby re-checks whether the problem cleared on its own.

Benefits and advantages

  • Customers hear back on issues that were already answered
  • One root cause is handled once, not once per Jira
  • Checks the ticket and the Jira are the same customer before drafting
  • Every send leaves a note on the ticket and a marker on the Jira
  • Read-only until a person approves the batch

CS Ops Dashboards

The live dashboards and tools GoKiwi's CS team runs on every day, built on Google Apps Script instead of paid SaaS.

Why it was built

Team leads had no live view of calls, response times, attendance or rosters, and the paid tools that offered one cost more than they were worth for a team this size.

What it does

Scheduled Apps Script jobs pull help desk, call and warehouse data into live dashboards for call operations, responses, attendance and rosters. Team lists, shifts and SLA rules are read from a sheet the team edits.

  • No paid seats; it runs on Google tools the team already had

Kiwi RM: live-chat AI

Kiwi's live-chat assistant: a chat layer that runs every conversation, one home for the SOPs, and an intelligence service that picks and runs the right SOP against Kiwi's systems.

38SOPs in the catalog
99.1%messages routed right, in 0.5 s
96.4%right SOP picked on the live catalog
6 to 8 sto the first reply

Measured before launch on 342 test messages.

Why it was built

Account problems in chat need the right SOP run against Kiwi's own systems, and a person when the bot is unsure. A single chatbot with one giant prompt gets worse as SOPs are added.

What it does

Takes each customer message from the LimeChat helpdesk and asks only for what the customer knows. The intelligence service picks and runs the SOP; the reply goes back in the brand voice and the customer's language, or the chat is handed to a person when no SOP fits.

Benefits and advantages

  • One home for SOPs; an edit goes live within 60 seconds
  • A crash or a deploy loses nothing: messages are saved first
  • Grows by adding identical containers, with no queue to run
  • Clear hand-over rules, and no chat waits more than 12 minutes
  • Every prompt version is kept

The chat layer owns the conversation but never tells the intelligence service which SOP to run. It sends the issue and what the customer said; the intelligence service picks and runs the SOPs and calls back. Both read the same SOPs from the SOP service.
LimeChat helpdesk
The middleman between the app's chat widget and the bot. It sends each new message by webhook and decides who owns the chat: the bot or a person.
Chat layer
Understands the message, asks only for what the customer knows, starts a run for the issue, and turns the result into a reply in the brand voice and the customer's language.
SOP service
The one place SOPs, templates and facts live, with every version, a review by a second person, and publishing.
Intelligence service
Built and hosted by Kiwi's tech team. It picks the SOPs for an issue, runs them against Kiwi's systems, files Jira once per issue and calls the chat layer back.

Background loop
Every 5 seconds: messages left unhandled, the 5-minute nudge, the 12-minute hand-over, and a status check for runs with no callback after 2 minutes.

Resume Studio

The console behind this site: one place to edit the resume and portfolio, with every resume version ready to download.

Why it was built

Keeping a resume, an ATS version and a portfolio in sync meant editing the same facts in several files and watching them drift apart.

What it does

An editor for every section of the resume and portfolio, saved to a private GitHub repo. Every resume version and the portfolio are drawn from that one file.

Benefits and advantages

  • One source of truth: a fact is edited once
  • Each save is a commit, so any version can be restored
  • 8 resume versions, including a real Word file
  • Refuses saves that look like a wipe
  • Only its owner can open the console
